sentence: Where the pronoun attaches, and what happens with verbs like *dormirse* and *quedarse* that use the same forms without a truly reflexive meaning, is covered in full in [Spanish reflexive verbs](/spanish-reflexive-verbs/).
note: Target explains infinitive attachment and nonreflexive dormirse/quedarse meanings; source does not assert every daily-routine se is a reflexive argument. Independent target findings about levantarse and every-me are forwarded to root/tail agent for correction. Actual target quotation: *dormirse* means to fall asleep

sentence: The [same unaccented spelling that separates *cuándo* the question word from *cuando* the connector](/spanish-accent-marks/) applies here too: *que* and *cual* only carry a written accent when they're asking or exclaiming something, never when they're doing this relative-clause job.
note: Target separates interrogative/exclamative cuándo from relative cuando; bridge applies this orthographic contrast to que/cual only, not all accent rules. Actual target quotation: No sé cuándo llega
